Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick ask — Acme wants logo + product photos for case study in exchange for 20% concession

Vanessa — thanks for the ping. High-level legal concerns and suggested guardrails:

1) Trademark/Logo placement: We can permit site placement for a fixed 12-month window. Require a brand usage approval flow (we sign-off on the exact creative prior to publish).

2) Product photos: We need written confirmation that Acme owns the images and that there are no third-party rights or subject-matter confidentiality. If images include identifiable third-party branding or customer data, we must require blurring/watermarking or refuse.

3) Case study content: Redwood must have a 5-business-day review and approval right on any public-facing materials. No statements that imply warranty or performance SLAs beyond the contract.

4) Attribution & timing: No exclusivity. If Acme wants a joint press release, we should require a joint PR plan and restrict any claim about discounts tied to marketing obligations.

5) Contract language: Add a limited marketing license (12 months), a moral-rights waiver for the case study language we approve, and a hold-harmless clause for imagery.

I'm attaching a short redline template I propose (I did not attach the binary file here — will drop redline in the shared Drive link).

If they're pressing for an accelerated timeline, we can offer conditional preliminary approval subject to the above items and a signature on a simple Marketing MOU.

— Marcus
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Adding a CS perspective: the robot arm photos are likely fine but may reveal floor layouts and partner logos (we've seen this before). Request that we require the following operational steps:
- Photos submitted for use go through a technical review (2 business days) to check for PII / partner branding.
- Any sensitive imagery must be cropped or blurred.
- If they want to share training data or logs in the case study, we must redact.

Also, Acme's stated 20% ask feels outside our normal promotional playbook for this ARR band — would like finance to weigh in on a counter-proposal.

Thanks,
Lauren
Director, Customer Success

Subject: Re: Quick ask — Acme wants logo + product photos for case study in exchange for 20% concession

Finance view: we ran the numbers on RW-ACME-2026-07 (attached in deal_summary.xlsx). A 20% one-year concession reduces LTV payback beyond our typical thresholds. Proposed counter-offer: 10% discount on year one if the customer commits to a co-branded case study + a joint webinar (we track registration goals).

Other conditions: discount contingent on signed Marketing MOU and a minimum 6-month run on the case study placement. Any additional creative rights (e.g., unlimited use of high-res product photos) should be priced as an add-on.

If Sales confirms marketing ROI metrics (HubSpot tracking), finance can consider flexible credit terms.

— Neha
Head of Revenue Finance
